name: Quad Set with Towel Roll
cues: Roll a small towel firmly under the knee so the joint rests on the roll
Tighten the thigh and press the back of the knee straight down into the towel
Keep the heel down and do not lift the hip to cheat the contraction

name: Straight Leg Raise (Supine)
cues: Lock the knee completely straight before the heel leaves the table
Lift only to the height of the opposite bent knee
Lower slowly and do not let the knee bend or the pelvis roll

name: Seated Superior Patellar Glide
cues: Sit with the knee fully extended and the quadriceps relaxed
Cup the inferior border of the patella with the web space of both hands
Glide the kneecap toward the hip without compressing it into the femur

name: Terminal Knee Extension (Band)
cues: Anchor the band behind the knee crease and step back to light tension
Straighten the knee fully so the band slides toward the joint line
Keep the knee over the second toe and do not lock the hip into a lean

name: Heel Slide
cues: Lie supine and place a sock or strap under the heel to reduce friction
Slide the heel toward the buttock until a firm, tolerable stretch
Keep the heel in line with the hip and do not let the knee fall outward

name: Long Arc Quad
cues: Sit tall with the thigh supported and the knee starting near 90 degrees
Straighten until the leg is level and the kneecap is pulled up
Lower through the last few degrees instead of dropping the foot
aliases: Double Leg Extension Holds On Machine At 0°
Full ROM Double Leg Extension On Machine

name: Side-Lying Clamshell
cues: Lie on the side with hips stacked and both knees bent about 45 degrees
Keep the heels together and lift the top knee without rolling the pelvis back
Stop before the low back twists; the motion stays in the hip

name: Supine Glute Bridge
cues: Lie hooklying with the feet hip-width and the heels close to the hips
Lift the pelvis until the shoulders, hips, and knees make one line
Keep the knees from splaying out or pinching together

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
cues: Lie on the side with the bottom knee bent and the top leg straight
Lead with the heel and lift the top leg slightly behind the trunk
Point the toes forward and do not hike the pelvis toward the ribs

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
cues: Half-kneel with the back knee under the hip and the front shin vertical
Tuck the pelvis so the belt buckle nods toward the ribs
Shift slightly forward until the stretch is in the front of the hip, not the low back

name: Figure-4 Piriformis Stretch
cues: Lie supine and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh just above the knee
Flex the foot and let the crossed knee open toward the side
Draw the uncrossed thigh in until the stretch is deep in the buttock

name: Prone Press-Up (McKenzie Extension)
cues: Lie prone with the hands under the shoulders and the legs fully relaxed
Press the chest up with the arms only; leave the pelvis on the table
Stop at the height that eases or centralizes symptoms, then lower with control

name: Supine Double Knee to Chest
cues: Lie supine and draw both knees toward the chest with the hands
Keep the head, neck, and shoulders relaxed on the table
Hug gently to open the low back without holding the breath

name: Bird Dog
cues: Start on hands and knees with the ribs stacked over a neutral pelvis
Reach the opposite arm and leg until they are level with the trunk
Do not let the low back sag or the pelvis rotate toward the moving leg

name: Dead Bug
cues: Lie supine with the hips and knees at 90 degrees and the low back gently set
Lower the opposite arm and leg only as far as the back stays quiet
Exhale as the limbs move and do not let the ribs flare

name: Pelvic Tilt
cues: Lie hooklying with the feet flat and the spine in a comfortable mid-position
Gently flatten the low back into the table by nodding the pelvis
Keep the motion small and do not lift the hips into a bridge

name: Side-Lying Open Book
cues: Lie on the side with the knees stacked and bent, arms reaching forward
Open the top arm so the chest rotates toward the ceiling
Keep the knees together so the rotation stays in the mid-back

name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
cues: Place the roller across the mid-back and support the head with the hands
Extend over the roller only through the thoracic spine
Do not let the low back arch or the neck crank backward

name: Quadruped Thread the Needle
cues: Start on hands and knees with the hands under the shoulders
Slide one arm under the chest and let that shoulder lower toward the floor
Keep the hips square so the twist stays in the upper back

name: Seated Chin Tuck with Retraction
cues: Sit tall and look straight ahead
Draw the chin straight back to make a double chin, without tipping down
Keep the chest up so the motion is at the neck, not a slump of the trunk

name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
cues: Sit tall and side-bend the ear toward the opposite shoulder
Let the stretching-side shoulder stay heavy and down
Use only a light hand assist and do not pull the head forward

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
cues: Turn the nose about 45 degrees toward the armpit
Nod the chin slightly down and let the stretching-side shoulder drop
The stretch should land at the angle of the neck and the top of the shoulder blade

name: Scapular Retraction and Depression
cues: Sit or stand tall with the arms relaxed at the sides
Slide the shoulder blades down and slightly together, toward the back pockets
Do not shrug, arch the low back, or pinch the blades hard

name: Standing Band Horizontal Abduction
cues: Hold the band at chest height with the hands about shoulder-width apart
Pull the hands apart and squeeze the shoulder blades together
Keep the shoulders down and the elbows softly bent

name: Band External Rotation at 0° with Towel Roll
cues: Pinch a small towel roll between the elbow and the ribs
Keep the elbow on the towel and rotate the forearm outward
Do not let the elbow drift forward or the shoulder hike

name: Sleeper Stretch
cues: Lie on the involved side with that shoulder flexed about 90 degrees
Gently press the forearm toward the table to rotate the shoulder inward
Stop at a stretch in the back of the shoulder; do not force a pinch in the front

name: Serratus Wall Slide with Band
cues: Face the wall with the forearms on the wall and a light band around the wrists
Slide the arms up while reaching the shoulder blades forward around the ribs
Keep the low back quiet and do not shrug as the arms rise

name: Wand Shoulder Flexion
cues: Hold a cane or dowel with both hands, thumbs up if comfortable
Use the uninvolved arm to lift the wand forward and overhead
Keep the ribs down and stop before the low back arches to gain height

name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
cues: Straighten the elbow and point the fingers toward the floor
Use the other hand to bend the wrist gently into flexion
Keep the shoulder relaxed so the stretch stays on the top of the forearm

name: Eccentric Wrist Extension
cues: Support the forearm on a table, palm down, with the wrist just past the edge
Use the other hand to lift the wrist, then lower slowly with the working hand
Make the lowering phase the work and do not let the wrist drop

name: Forearm Pronation and Supination with Hammer
cues: Hold a hammer at the end of the handle with the elbow tucked to the side
Rotate the palm up and palm down through a comfortable arc
Keep the elbow still so the motion comes from the forearm, not the shoulder

name: Tendon Gliding (Hook, Straight Fist, Full Fist)
cues: Start with the fingers straight, then make a hook fist with the large knuckles straight
Move to a straight fist, then a full fist, pausing briefly in each shape
Keep the wrist neutral and do not force a painful end range

name: First Web Space Stretch
cues: Open the thumb away from the index finger to widen the web space
Assist at the base of the thumb, not by levering the tip
Keep the wrist neutral and do not hyperextend the thumb joints

name: Putty Grip Squeeze
cues: Hold therapy putty in the palm and wrap the fingers fully around it
Squeeze and hold, then release without flicking the wrist
Keep the thumb opposed so the grip is a full fist, not a pinch

name: Standing Gastrocnemius Wall Stretch
cues: Place the back foot straight ahead with the heel down and the knee locked
Lean the hips toward the wall until the stretch is in the upper calf
Do not let the arch collapse or the foot turn out

name: Standing Soleus Wall Stretch
cues: Use the same staggered stance, then bend the back knee while the heel stays down
Let the stretch shift lower, toward the Achilles
Keep the knee tracking over the second toe

name: 4-Way Ankle with Elastic Band
cues: Sit with the ankle free and the band set to resist the direction you are working
Move only at the ankle: pull up, point down, turn in, and turn out
Keep the knee still so the shin muscles, not the hip, do the work

name: Standing Heel Raise (Double to Single Leg)
cues: Stand at a counter with the feet hip-width and the knees soft
Rise onto the balls of the feet with weight through the big-toe side
Lower slowly, and use one leg only when two-leg raises stay steady

name: Single-Leg Stance
cues: Stand near a counter and shift your weight fully onto one leg
Keep the pelvis level and the stance knee softly unlocked
Look at a fixed point; light fingertip support is allowed at first

name: Tandem Romberg Stance with Head Turns
cues: Place one foot directly in front of the other so the heel touches the toe
Turn the head slowly side to side without stepping out of the stance
Keep the hips square and let the eyes move with the head

name: Lateral Weight Shift on Airex Pad
cues: Stand on the foam pad with the feet hip-width and the knees soft
Shift weight slowly from one foot to the other without hiking the pelvis
Keep the trunk upright so the correction stays at the hips and ankles

name: Quadruped Transverse Abdominis Drawing-In
cues: On hands and knees, set a neutral spine with the ribs over the pelvis
Draw the lower abdomen up and in, as if tightening a belt one notch
Keep breathing; do not tuck the pelvis hard or hold the breath

name: Side Plank from Knees
cues: Lie on the side, prop on the forearm, and bend both knees
Lift the hips until the shoulder, hip, and knees line up
Stack the top shoulder over the supporting shoulder and do not roll the hips forward

name: Supine Marching with Core Brace
cues: Lie hooklying and brace so the low back stays gently set on the table
Lift one foot a few inches, then set it down before the other leg moves
If the pelvis rocks, lift less high

name: Modified Thomas Stretch
cues: Sit at the edge of the table, then roll back and hug one knee to the chest
Let the other thigh hang off the table until a stretch is felt at the front of the hip
Keep the low back flat on the table and do not let the hanging thigh swing out

name: Supine Bridge
cues: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat
Lift the hips until the shoulders, hips, and knees line up
Lower slowly and keep the ribs down so the low back does not arch

name: Mini Squat with Counter Support
cues: Hold the counter lightly and stand with feet about hip width
Bend both knees a short distance while keeping the heels down
Stand back up through the heels without locking the knees hard

name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
cues: Sit tall with the stretching leg straight and the other foot supported
Hinge forward from the hips until a stretch is felt behind the thigh
Keep the knee soft-straight and do not round hard through the low back

name: Supine Gluteal Sets
cues: Lie on your back with legs relaxed
Squeeze both buttocks together without arching the low back
Hold the contraction, then fully relax before the next one

name: Seated Table Hamstring Stretch
cues: Sit at the edge of the table with one leg straight along the surface
Sit tall, then hinge forward from the hips until the back of the thigh stretches
Keep the foot relaxed and do not bounce at the end of the motion

name: Squat
cues: Stand with feet about hip width and weight through the heels
Sit the hips back and down while the knees track over the toes
Keep the chest up and stand by driving through both heels
aliases: TRX Assisted Squats On Wedge With

name: Supine Hip Adduction Isometric with Ball
cues: Lie on your back with knees bent and a ball between the knees
Squeeze the ball gently and keep the pelvis still
Hold the squeeze, then release without letting the knees fall open

name: Bridge with Hip Abduction and Resistance
cues: Lie on your back with knees bent and a band above the knees
Press the knees slightly apart as you lift the hips
Lower with control and keep the band tension even

name: Forward Step Up
cues: Place the whole foot on the step and keep the knee tracking over the toes
Drive through the heel to stand tall without pushing off the back foot
Lower with control until the back foot taps down

name: Prone Hip Extension
cues: Lie face down with both hips resting on the table
Lift one straight leg a few inches without rolling the pelvis
Lower slowly and keep the low back quiet

name: Side Stepping with Resistance at Ankles
cues: Stand tall with a slight knee bend and the band just above the ankles
Step sideways while keeping the pelvis level and the toes forward
Do not let the trailing leg drag or the trunk lean

name: Side Stepping with Resistance at Feet
cues: Stand tall with a slight knee bend and the band around the feet
Step sideways leading with the heel and keep the toes forward
Control the return step so the knees do not collapse inward

name: Prone Hip Extension on Table
cues: Lie face down with the hips at the edge of the table and the trunk supported
Lift one leg toward the ceiling only as far as the pelvis stays still
Lower slowly and avoid arching the low back to get higher

name: Hip Abduction with Resistance Loop
cues: Stand tall with a loop around the thighs and a soft knee bend
Step or press the leg out to the side without leaning the trunk
Return slowly and keep the pelvis level

name: Hip Extension with Resistance Loop
cues: Stand tall with a loop around the ankles and a light hold for balance
Reach one leg back against the band without arching the low back
Return with control and keep the stance knee soft

name: Seated Inferior Patellar Glide
cues: Sit with the knee relaxed and the thigh supported
Cup the top of the kneecap and glide it gently toward the foot
Use a comfortable pressure and do not force the kneecap into the joint

name: Hooklying Single Knee to Chest Stretch
cues: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the foot flat
Draw the other knee toward the chest until a gentle low-back stretch is felt
Keep the head and shoulders relaxed and do not pull through pain

name: Standing Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Resistance
cues: Stand tall and hold the band with the arms in front at shoulder height
Pull the hands apart and squeeze the shoulder blades together
Return slowly and keep the shoulders down away from the ears

name: Bridge with Heels on Swiss Ball
cues: Lie on your back with both heels on the ball and knees straight
Lift the hips until the body is a straight line from shoulders to heels
Keep the ball steady and lower the hips without dropping them

name: Lunge Matrix on Slider
cues: Stand tall with the moving foot on the slider
Slide into one direction of the lunge, then return to the start before changing direction
Keep the standing knee tracking over the toes and the trunk upright

name: Lateral Lunge with Slider
cues: Stand tall with one foot on the slider
Shift the hips toward the standing leg as the slider foot glides out
Push through the standing heel to return, keeping the knee over the toes

name: Lunge on Slider
cues: Stand tall with the back foot on the slider
Lower into a lunge as the back foot slides, keeping the front knee over the toes
Press through the front heel to return to standing

name: Clamshell with Resistance
cues: Lie on your side with a band above the knees and the feet together
Lift the top knee against the band while the pelvis stays stacked
Lower with control and keep the low back quiet

name: Sidelying Hip Adduction
cues: Lie on your side with the top leg bent and the foot placed in front
Lift the bottom leg a few inches without rolling the pelvis
Lower slowly and keep the toes pointing forward

name: Lunge Matrix
cues: Stand tall with the moving foot ready to step
Lunge in one direction, then return to the start before changing direction
Keep the front knee tracking over the toes and the trunk upright

name: Long Sitting Isometric Hip Adduction and Extension with Ball at Knees
cues: Sit tall with the legs out and a ball between the knees
Squeeze the ball and press the thighs down into the surface
Hold the contraction, then relax without rounding the low back

name: Supine Lower Trunk Rotation
cues: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat
Slowly roll both knees to one side while the shoulders stay down
Return to the middle and repeat to the other side

name: Prone Press-Up on Elbows
cues: Lie face down and prop on your elbows under the shoulders
Let the low back sag gently while the hips stay on the table
Hold the comfortable extension, then rest back down

name: Side Plank on Elbow
cues: Lie on your side and prop on the elbow under the shoulder
Lift the hips so the body makes a straight line
Keep the neck long and do not let the hips roll forward

name: Standing Lumbar Extension
cues: Stand tall with the feet about hip width
Place the hands on the hips and gently arch the low back
Return upright without forcing the motion

name: Child's Pose Stretch
cues: Kneel and sit the hips back toward the heels
Reach the arms forward and let the chest sink toward the floor
Breathe and keep the stretch comfortable through the back

name: Supine Piriformis Stretch with Foot on Ground
cues: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh
Keep the foot of the supporting leg on the ground
Draw the thigh in until a stretch is felt deep in the buttock

name: Mountain Climbers, Slow
cues: Start in a plank with the hands under the shoulders
Step one knee toward the chest, then switch legs slowly
Keep the hips level and do not bounce

name: Standing Diagonal Chops with Medicine Ball
cues: Stand with a soft knee bend and hold the ball at one shoulder
Chop the ball diagonally down across the body
Control the return and keep the trunk from collapsing

name: Plank on Knees
cues: Prop on the forearms with the knees on the floor
Make a straight line from the head to the knees
Brace the stomach and do not let the low back sag

name: Bent Knee Fallouts
cues: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet together
Let one knee fall out to the side while the pelvis stays still
Bring the knee back to the middle with control

name: Supine Transversus Abdominis Bracing
cues: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the hands on the lower stomach
Gently draw the belly in without holding your breath
Keep the ribs down and the low back quiet

name: Sidelying TFL Stretch
cues: Lie on your side with the bottom leg straight
Let the top leg drop behind you until the outer hip stretches
Keep the pelvis stacked and do not twist the low back

name: Standing Ulnar Nerve Glide
cues: Stand tall and make the 'OK' sign with the thumb and index finger
Bring the hand toward the face, then turn it out like a mask
Move only as far as a gentle nerve glide, not a strong stretch

name: Standard Plank
cues: Prop on the forearms and toes with the body in one line
Brace the stomach and squeeze the glutes
Do not let the hips pike up or the low back sag

name: Seated Lumbar Extension
cues: Sit tall at the front of a chair with the feet supported
Gently arch the low back and lift the chest
Return upright without forcing the motion

name: Supine Isometric Hamstring Set
cues: Lie on your back with the knee slightly bent
Press the heel down as if you are trying to bend the knee
Hold the hamstring contraction, then relax

name: Thomas Stretch on Table
cues: Sit at the edge of the table and roll back while hugging one knee
Let the other thigh hang off the table
Keep the low back flat and feel the stretch in the front of the hanging hip

name: Modified Side Plank with Hip Abduction
cues: Set up in a side plank from the knees
Lift the top leg a few inches without rolling the trunk
Lower the leg with control and keep the hips lifted

name: Half-Kneeling Diagonal Chops with Medicine Ball
cues: Half kneel with the front knee over the ankle
Chop the ball from the high side down across the body
Stay tall and do not let the front knee cave in

name: Bird Dog on Foam Roll
cues: Rest the shins or hands on the roll as directed and find a tall spine
Reach the opposite arm and leg until they are level with the trunk
Move slowly and do not let the low back sag

name: Half-Kneeling Diagonal Lift with Resistance
cues: Half kneel with the band starting low on the side of the back leg
Lift the hands diagonally up across the body
Keep the ribs stacked and the front knee over the foot

name: Swiss Ball March
cues: Lie on your back with the heels on the ball and the hips lifted
March one foot, then the other, without dropping the hips
Keep the ribs down and the motion slow

name: Full Superman on Table
cues: Lie face down with the arms reaching overhead
Lift the arms, chest, and legs a few inches off the table
Lower slowly and do not crank the neck back

name: Single-Leg Bridge with Leg Supported
cues: Lie on your back with one foot on the floor and the other leg supported
Lift the hips by pushing through the standing heel
Keep the pelvis level and lower with control

name: Standing Sidebends
cues: Stand tall with the arms at the sides
Slide one hand down the thigh as the trunk bends sideways
Return to the middle and repeat to the other side

name: Prone Knee Extension Hang
cues: Lie face down with the knee just past the edge of the table
Let the lower leg hang so the knee straightens with gravity
Stay relaxed and do not force the knee down

name: Gentle Levator Scapulae Stretch
cues: Sit tall and look down toward the opposite armpit
Use a light hand pressure only if it stays comfortable
Keep the stretch in the back of the neck, not the shoulder joint

name: Seated Cervical Rotation AROM
cues: Sit tall and look over one shoulder as far as is comfortable
Return to the middle, then turn to the other side
Move slowly and keep the shoulders relaxed

name: Seated Cervical Extension AROM
cues: Sit tall and look up only as far as the neck stays comfortable
Return to a neutral chin position
Do not force the head backward

name: Seated Cervical Flexion AROM
cues: Sit tall and nod the chin toward the chest
Return to neutral without jutting the chin forward
Keep the motion slow and pain free

name: Seated Cervical Sidebending AROM
cues: Sit tall and tilt one ear toward the same shoulder
Return to the middle, then tilt to the other side
Keep the shoulders down and do not rotate the head

name: Standing Pendulum
cues: Lean forward and support the body with the uninvolved arm.
Let the involved arm hang and make small circles.
Keep the shoulder relaxed.

name: Supine Passive External Rotation
cues: Lie on your back and hold a wand with both hands.
Let the uninvolved arm roll the involved forearm outward.
Stop at the first stretch or the surgeon's limit.

name: Band Internal Rotation at 0°
cues: Elbow at 90 degrees at side, rotate inward across stomach.

name: Standing Scaption (Full Can)
cues: Raise arms in scapular plane (30 deg forward of coronal plane), thumbs up, stop at 90 deg.
